I want you to research what we can make for a quick and fun sort of cash grab, Gatcha and loot box mechanic, genre mixing, mobile game, which you are able to fully code and compile for me, which we can then distribute on the Google Play store, integrating vercel and supabase, Database Oriented Design, all the coding tricks and tools in whatever language you find best based on your research into market trends and genre staples as well as up and coming games and ideas. Use Scholar Gateway as needed, research, and come up with a plan, then we will build the design documents and materials and get them over to your coding counterpart. It is Feb 2026, we will be using Visual Studio Code with Claude Opus 4.6. Also, bear in mind that I don't have a core idea for the gameplay loop, this will be something we can crank out while I work on a larger project to help with funds, so I need you to look into as well what makes the top mobile games fun and engaging and synthesize a game with that in mind. Also bear in mind that Claude Opus 4.6 in Visual Studio Code will be building this from start to finish, as hands-off as possible, so it needs to remain feasible from that perspective. Make it easy enough on yourself to do this yet complex enough to remain engaging and with the tech stack to match! You are writing instructions for your own coding counterpart essentially. The primary revenue driver will be the Gatcha/Lootboxes and Battlepass/cosmetics, absolutely no ads.

Great project — this is right up my alley given those uploaded docs and the constraints. Before I dive into deep research, a few quick clarifications to make sure the research is laser-focused:

1. **What's your target timeline?** Are we talking 4-6 weeks, 2-3 months, or flexible?
2. **Art style / asset budget** — are you open to AI-generated 2D art (which Claude can integrate more easily), or do you have an artist? This heavily affects what genres are feasible for a hands-off build.
3. **Any genre hard no's?** For example, would you rule out idle/clicker games, card battlers, tower defense, etc.?

Perfect — flexible timeline, AI-generated 2D art, no tower defense or idle/clicker. That gives us a lot of room. Time to do a deep dive into mobile market trends, gacha mechanics, genre-mixing strategies, and what's feasible for a Claude Opus 4.6 + VSCode hands-off build pipeline. Let me kick off the research now.
Please proceed.
Please proceed.
Please proceed.

Please proceed.

The deep research is currently running — it's digging through market data, tech stack feasibility, gacha design patterns, and everything else we need. This kind of comprehensive sweep usually takes a few minutes.

While we wait, I'll also review your uploaded design documents so I can cross-reference your existing game design thinking with whatever the research surfaces. That way the final synthesis will incorporate both market intelligence and your own design frameworks.

Good — I've now reviewed all six of your design documents. Here's what I'm pulling from them that's relevant to our mobile gacha project:

**From your docs that we can leverage:**
- **Database-Oriented Design** philosophy (Roguelike Architecture doc) — perfect for Supabase
- **ECS-style component composition** for defining gacha units/characters as data, not classes
- **Procedural 2D asset generation** techniques (SDF-based rendering, Wave Function Collapse)
- **Storylet-based narrative system** — lightweight, tag-driven quest/event system perfect for daily content
- **The "Automation Curve" engagement model** — shifting player effort from manual to strategic over time
- **"Low Floor, High Ceiling" design** — accessible but deep, critical for mobile retention

The deep research is still running. Once it returns with market data, tech stack validation, and trending genre analysis, I'll synthesize everything into a comprehensive game concept and build plan. Hang tight — this is going to be a thorough document.
How is the research coming along?

The research task is still processing — these deep dives typically take a few minutes given the breadth of what we asked it to cover (market trends, gacha mechanics, tech stack feasibility, Google Play requirements, art pipelines, and genre synthesis all in one sweep).

In the meantime, here's where we stand with what I've already gathered from your uploaded documents:

**Key frameworks I've extracted that directly apply to our mobile gacha project:**

Your Roguelike Architecture doc gives us a solid **Database-Oriented Design** blueprint — characters, items, and gacha units defined as rows in relational tables rather than class hierarchies. This maps perfectly onto Supabase/PostgreSQL. A gacha character becomes a composition of rows across tables (BaseUnit + Rarity + Element + Skills) rather than a monolithic object, which makes the pull system trivially data-driven.

Your Designing Engaging Game Systems doc has the **"Automation Curve"** concept and the "Low Floor, High Ceiling" principle — both critical for a mobile game that needs to hook in 30 seconds but retain for months. The idea that player effort shifts from *doing* to *designing strategy* is exactly the autobattler/team-comp loop that prints money in gacha.

Your Procedural 2D Graphics doc gives us techniques for generating visual variety from code (SDF compositing, WFC for tilemap variety), which could help stretch AI-generated art assets further.

I'll ping you the moment the research lands and then we'll synthesize everything into the game concept and build plan. Shouldn't be much longer.
It says something went wrong, the research may have stalled and may need to be restarted.

No worries — let me relaunch it right now. Same comprehensive scope.

Your mobile gacha game blueprint is ready. It covers the $80.9B mobile market opportunity, recommends a roguelite auto-battler collector as the optimal game concept, and details the full tech stack (Phaser.js + Capacitor + Supabase + Vercel). The report includes gacha monetization design based on the HoYoverse pity model, regional regulatory requirements through 2026, an AI art production pipeline using ComfyUI with anime LoRAs, and Google Play distribution requirements including Billing Library 7.0+ compliance.

The graphics should be SVG, high-count primitive based, proc-gen, yet highly detailed, anime-inspired. Let's move away from Google Play and make it purely web based if that gives a better tech-stack and code capabilities. I also don't want to deal with the Google regulations now that you mention it. One of my design documents I uploaded detailed the proc-gen 2D graphics, we want 2D vector based assets that mimic hand drawn 2.5D art.

I want it to be engaging and intuitive while maintaining complexity and still being easy enough for Claude Opus 4.6 in Visual Studio Code to be able to develop with minimal input from me, did you integrate your findings from my design docs into this as well? Do you need to do additional research with these new needs?

Great call on all fronts — web-only removes a massive layer of friction (no Capacitor, no Google Play Billing, no AAB builds, no app store review), and SVG proc-gen is a brilliant fit for AI-coded development since it's literally code generating art. Let me dive deeper into your Procedural 2D Graphics doc since that's now the cornerstone of the visual system, and then I'll do targeted research on the web-only stack changes.

Now let me do targeted research on the web-only pivot and SVG proc-gen game rendering.

I now have everything I need. The pivot to web-only + SVG proc-gen actually *dramatically improves* the entire project — simpler tech stack, no app store fees (Stripe's 2.9% vs Google's 15-30%), no regulations to navigate, and SVG is literally code generating art which is exactly what Claude Opus 4.6 excels at. Let me write the comprehensive updated blueprint.

Now let me build the comprehensive design blueprint document — this will be the master reference for both you and your coding counterpart.

Here's your complete blueprint. To directly answer your questions:

**Yes, I deeply integrated your design docs.** Specifically:

- **Procedural 2D Graphics doc** → The entire SVG art system is built on your SDF boolean algebra (Section 1.2 → SVG clipPath/mask composition for weapons), L-Systems (Section 5 → hair generation), WFC (Section 2 → dungeon tilemap layouts), and the Text-to-Parameter pipeline (Section 6.1 → seed-based parameter derivation for items)

- **Roguelike Architecture doc** → The Database-Oriented Design principle ("the fundamental unit is the Data Table, not the Object") drives the entire Supabase schema. Heroes, relics, and items are relational data compositions, not class hierarchies. The ECS philosophy maps to PostgreSQL tables + JSONB components.

- **Designing Engaging Game Systems doc** → The "Automation Curve" principle shapes combat (players *design strategy*, not *perform actions*). The "Low Floor, High Ceiling" concept drives the auto-battle-with-positioning system. The "Eureka moment" design feeds into elemental reaction discovery.

**The key pivot decisions:**

1. **SVG → Canvas hybrid** solves the performance problem (SVG DOM dies at 3-5K elements, but we rasterize to Canvas textures at load time and use live SVG only for showcase moments like gacha reveals)

2. **Web-only + Stripe** saves 12-27% on every transaction vs Google Play, eliminates all app store regulatory burden, and actually *simplifies* the codebase (no Capacitor, no native bridge, no AAB builds)

3. **"Eidolon Rift" as a roguelite auto-battler collector** is the optimal genre mashup because procedural generation creates infinite content from finite code, auto-combat eliminates complex input systems, and the gacha hero roster is pure data

Want me to adjust anything in the concept, pivot the genre, tweak the monetization model, or start building specific design documents (like the full hero roster, relic catalog, or detailed SVG generation specifications)?

I want there to be tons of variety in the Hero roster and relics, while maintaining good differentiation between them, something like 50 heroes seems good enough for most mobile games but I want a LOT, I want it to feel like a BIG game. Let's start the design documents as you suggested, and any others you can think of to get as granular with this as possible to make it easier on VS Code Claude, do any additional research needed as you go to make them in-depth.

Actually... What about something almost NFT-like in that Heroes and Relics are also generated procedurally from many components or rules since we are going with a DOD approach and a database? We could have a nigh-infinite roster...

That's a *brilliant* pivot — and it fundamentally elevates the entire project. Instead of a fixed roster where everyone has the same characters, every player's collection is genuinely unique. The gacha pull doesn't ask "will I get Character X?" — it asks "what one-of-a-kind hero will the Rift generate for me?" That's a fundamentally more compelling collector's fantasy.

Let me do some targeted research on procedural character generation systems and trait-based composition in games, then I'll build out the full design document suite.
